title: Variability Portrait: per-model & per-route performance canvases
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: Design a compact, scannable performance 'Variability Portrait' canvas for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route behavior across latency, throughput, and token metrics. This spec focuses on layout patterns, chart stacking rules, interaction states, and handoff artifacts for engineering. It is intentionally different from existing 'timeline' and 'sparkline' canvases: the Variability Portrait emphasizes distribution-aware visuals (violin + percentile bands), trend coherence (rolling median + stability band), and cost attribution per token bucket to make regression causes visible at a glance.

Goals:
- Help devs quickly decide if an observed spike is systemic (model-level), route-specific, or due to token distribution shifts.
- Make cost/latency trade-offs explicit: show cost-per-token percentiles and hot-path contribution.
- Support quick drill-down to token-level microtraces and rollout history.

Canvas components and rules (compact, left-to-right scan):
1) Header strip (compact): model name, route name, last deploy tag, current SLO badge (green/amber/red), and quick actions (pin, compare, open rollout).
2) Variability lane (left): Vertical violin plot representing token-latency distribution for selected window (90m/6h/24h). Overlays: rolling median (solid line), p50/p90/p99 markers (dots), and a translucent 15–85% stability band. Violin width encodes relative request volume.
3) Throughput lane (center): Hourly throughput mini-heatmap (small multiples per day) with color scale anchored to route peak. Tooltip shows requests/min and burst factor (current/avg). A sparkline above shows rolling RPS.
4) Token-cost lane (right): Stacked area showing cost-per-token percentiles (p10/p50/p90 slices) and cumulative spend annotation. Hovering a percentile isolates that slice and highlights related latency violin segments.
5) Token flow microtrace link: inline CTA that opens a token waterfall modal with top 3 prefixes contributing to latency/cost regression.
6) Anomalies & rollout timeline row (bottom): compact swimlane that shows anomalies (auto-detected by Optimize) and rollout markers; clicking a rollout filters the whole canvas to pre/post windows.

Interaction design and microcopy rules:
- Hover on violin: show distribution histogram, sample count, and median/pX values. Copy: "Median 72ms • p90 210ms • 12.3k requests".
- Click violin band: open quick-filter menu: isolate time window, compare to baseline model variant, or open probe on infra metrics.
- Hover on cost slice: tooltip shows itemized charges (compute, memory, storage, infra allocation).
- Keyboard nav: left/right moves between routes in the same model; up/down switches model. Esc closes modals.
- Empty-state: when request volume < 50 in window show a gentle hint: "Low sample size — try 24h or compare to sibling routes" and a CTA to open sampling guidance.

Chart specs (pixel-agnostic, relative sizing):
- Violin: vertical, normalized height = 120px, width = proportional to volume capped at 220px. Kernel density smoothing: Epanechnikov, bandwidth = Silverman rule of thumb. Density y-axis = latency (ms) log-scale optional toggle. Data buckets: 100 bins.
- Rolling median: 1.5px solid, brand-600 color. P50/p90/p99 markers: 6px filled circles with subtle drop shadow. Stability band: 24% opacity brand-200 fill between 15/85 percentiles.
- Throughput heatmap: grid cell = 8px square, gap 2px, color ramp uses perceptually-uniform Viridis-like palette. Legend shows percent of daily peak.
- Cost stacks: percentiles drawn as stacked polygons, anti-aliased edges, area baseline anchored to zero. Percentile boundaries annotated with thin dashed lines on hover.

Data/implementation notes for handoff:
- Primary backend signal: per-request trace with fields {timestamp, model_id, route_id, latency_ms, token_count, token_prefix_hash, cost_units}. Engineering should pre-aggregate: distributions (pX, histogram), rolling median time series, and percentile-bucketed cost summaries.
- Suggested precompute cadence: 1m for medians and histograms, 5m for full violin bucket rollups.
- Memory/cost trade-off: keep raw token microtraces only for 72h; longer retention via sampled summaries.

Acceptance criteria (design review + UX QA + Eng):
- Design spec scanned and approved by PM + Lead Eng (see comments).
- Figma prototype for desktop and compact tablet states with interactive violin hover and rollout timeline. Link included below.
- Engineering can render violin from the agreed histogram schema; perf tests show rendering < 120ms for 50 simultaneous canvases.
- Accessibility: color contrast passes AA; violin and percentile markers have text labels on focus; keyboard navigation validated.

Artifacts and links:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/placeholder/variability-portrait-proto (prototype v3)
- PRD / rationale: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Variability+Portrait+PRD
- Engineering ticket (suggested): ENG-20892 (notes in comments)
- Example GH PR that wires up histogram API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3245

Open decisions and trade-offs to resolve in review:
- Whether to use log-scale for latency by default (pro: better p99 separation; con: less intuitive for non-SREs). Recommend default = linear with a toggle for log.
- Violin smoothing level: tuned for median stability vs. noisy tails. We recommend adaptive smoothing (wider kernel when samples < 500).
- Cost attribution granularity: hourly slices vs. percentile slices. Initial rollout uses percentile slices for clearer median/p99 comparisons.

Next steps and handoff checklist:
- PM to confirm SLO definitions and threshold mapping (action: Jordan Patel).
- Lead Eng (Priya Rao) to validate histogram schema and retention assumptions.
- Prototype review session scheduled with Product and Observability Eng on 2026-03-16.
- Design QA: copy, micro-interactions, focus states, and keyboard flows finalized by 2026-03-20.

Notes for reviewers: this canvas is meant to complement existing timeline and sparkline primitives — it should not replace them. The Variability Portrait is optimized for root-cause triage and cost-contrast conversations between SREs and product teams.
